title: Hermes Skill Contract
description: A versioned, falsifiable contract for a Hermes skill. Ports the Skill-V (phi, p, rho, nu) shape (arXiv:2610.11781) over SkillOps' executable-artifact discipline (arXiv:2605.13716), with Hermes-specific additions: difficulty-bucketed outcome evidence and a human-review decision-aid gate. See skill-contract-schema.md for field-by-field rationale and worked examples.

skill_id.description: Stable identifier matching the skill's directory name (e.g. 'pdf', 'github-code-review'). Never changes across versions; a renamed skill is a new skill_id with a migration note in lineage.deprecates.

skill_version.description: SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH of the skill's procedure/scope (the p_i and phi_i parts). See 'Version bump policy' in the prose doc.

rubric_version.description: SemVer of outcome_criteria alone. Increments independently of skill_version — a skill can get several rubric revisions (tightened thresholds, new assertions) before its procedure changes at all, matching Skill-V Table 8's 'Skill v1->v2; Rubric v2->v3' pattern.

preconditions.description: Machine-checkable facts that MUST hold before the skill is invoked. Each is a boolean check, not prose, so a router/orchestrator can evaluate the whole list without invoking the skill.

kind.description: The class of mechanical check a worker/orchestrator runs to evaluate this precondition.

target.description: What the check operates on: a tool name, env var name, file glob, credential key, JSON Schema $id, or shell command.

args.description: Optional kind-specific parameters (e.g. timeout, expected exit code, schema inline).

hard.description: If true, failing this precondition means the skill MUST NOT be invoked (router hard-fails). If false, it's an advisory/soft precondition the invoker may override with justification logged in the trajectory.

applicability.description: Where this skill is valid to apply — the phi_i of Skill-V. Distinct from preconditions: preconditions are 'can I invoke right now' (environment state); applicability is 'is this skill even the right tool for this kind of task' (task/context scope). Both are evaluated before invocation, but applicability is what gates which evidence trajectories are allowed into this skill's replay buffer for outcome scoring (see outcome_criteria.evidence_scope).

task_types.description: Closed or open tag vocabulary describing the kinds of task this skill applies to, e.g. ['pdf.fill-form', 'pdf.extract-text']. An orchestrator matches a task's declared type(s) against this list; no match => skill is not a candidate.

input_schema_ref.description: Optional pointer (file path or $id) to a JSON Schema the task's input must validate against for this skill to be considered applicable. Objectively checkable via schema validation, not judgment.

excluded_contexts.description: Explicit negative scope — contexts where this skill looks applicable by task_types but is known NOT to apply (e.g. ['encrypted-pdf-without-password', 'scanned-image-only-pdf']). Required field (can be empty array) so authors are forced to think about known-bad territory rather than leaving it implicit.

protected_constraints.description: Semantic invariants that NO revision (of any version) may alter without a MAJOR skill_version bump — e.g. 'never writes outside the task workspace', 'never executes model-generated code'. Ported directly from Skill-V's phi_i protected semantic constraints (App. B.2). These are the diff the Evidence Gate checks for exact preservation on MINOR/PATCH bumps (see outcome_criteria.non_regression).

outcome_criteria.description: The executable rubric rho_i. Every criterion names an evidence_matcher — a fixed, deterministic grading function — so 'did this skill succeed' is answered by re-running a check, not by re-reading prose. This is what makes the contract falsifiable instead of aspirational.

hard_constraints.description: Binary gates. ANY failure here means the invocation is scored FAIL regardless of weighted score (mirrors Skill-V's H(tau)=0 gate term in ŷ_rub = 1[q(tau)>=eta AND H(tau)=0]).

weighted_criteria.description: Soft, weighted criteria whose weighted sum is compared to pass_threshold. Mirrors Skill-V's C_i = {c_ij}.

pass_threshold.description: Minimum weighted-criteria score (weights normalized to sum to 1) required to pass, given all hard_constraints already passed. Skill-V's eta=0.7 is the literature default; Hermes authors set this per skill.

difficulty_bucket.description: Hermes addition not present in either source paper (synthesis note section b flags that neither paper normalizes for task difficulty). Each recorded trajectory used as evidence MUST be tagged with a difficulty bucket; pass/fail rates and the non_regression check below are computed per-bucket, not pooled, so a skill cannot look healthy by being scored only on trivial tasks or look broken by being scored only on hard ones.

min_sample_per_bucket.description: Minimum number of evidence trajectories required in a difficulty bucket before that bucket's pass rate is trusted for maintenance decisions (retirement, promotion, revision gating). Explicitly fills the gap flagged in the synthesis note (section d): SkillOps gives no minimum-sample guard at all.

non_regression.description: The Evidence Gate (Skill-V Eq. 7, synthesis note section c). A candidate revision to outcome_criteria is only accepted if, replayed over the SAME stored evidence trajectories, it does not regress on any of these metrics, and protected_constraints are preserved exactly.

metrics.description: disc_rate must not increase, false_negative_rate must not increase, balanced_accuracy must not decrease, relative to the prior rubric_version, on the stored replay buffer.

replay_buffer_size.description: Number of stored (trajectory, rubric_judgment, actual_outcome) tuples retained for replay. Must be >= evidence_scope.min_sample_per_bucket * number of buckets in use.

lineage.description: Audit trail, ported from Skill-V's nu_i (Table 7/8): skill version, rubric version, traceability, update reason, evidence case identifiers.

previous_version.description: The skill_version this record supersedes, or null for the first version of a skill.

update_reason.description: Free-text but mandatory: why this version exists (e.g. 'tightened hard_constraints after false-positive on encrypted PDFs, evidence case ec-0042').

evidence_case_ids.description: Identifiers of specific trajectories/incidents that motivated this change. Empty array only permitted for the very first version of a skill (no history yet).

reviewed_by.description: Optional: identity (human or 'automated-gate-only') of whoever approved the change. See 'Human review' note in the prose doc for why this is not purely automated by default in Hermes, unlike both source papers.

deprecates.description: skill_id values this version supersedes/renames, if any (migration marker).

retirement_state.description: Hermes addition, not in either source paper as a working mechanism (SkillOps hard-deletes with an unverifiable threshold; Skill-V has none at all — synthesis note section d). Archive-first, never hard-delete from this schema's perspective: a retired skill's record persists with status='archived'.

candidate_reason.description: Why this skill was flagged (e.g. 'utility < 0.1 over last 30 evidence cases AND a red/duplicate skill exists').

min_sample_met.description: Whether evidence_scope.min_sample_per_bucket was satisfied before this status was set — a retirement decision made without this true is invalid.

weight.description: Required for weighted_criteria entries (ignored/omitted for hard_constraints, which are implicitly all-or-nothing).

evidence_matcher.description: The objective, re-runnable check that decides whether this criterion held for a given trajectory. Every 'kind' maps to a deterministic procedure — including llm_judge_rubric, which is pinned to a fixed model/prompt/threshold so the same trajectory always yields the same verdict, not open-ended judgment.

target.description: What is being checked (file path, output field, command).

expected.description: Expected value/pattern/schema reference, shape depends on kind.

params.description: kind-specific parameters, e.g. {model, prompt_ref, threshold} for llm_judge_rubric or {command, timeout_s} for external_command_assert.
